title: Two wallets
scenario: Two wallets, A and B. Put n coins in A only, then print both balances.

intro.job: Two wallets, A and B. Put n coins in A only, then print both balances.

idea.rule: Class attributes are the shared whiteboard; self. attributes are each wallet's own label — write on the wrong one and everyone sees it.
idea.detail: Anything set directly in the class body (balance = 0) belongs to the class — every wallet reads the same one. self.balance = 0 inside __init__ runs once per new wallet and gives THAT wallet its own balance. Inside a method, self.balance means 'this wallet's balance'; Wallet.balance means 'the shared one'.

model_restatement: Make two wallets, put coins in wallet A only, and show both balances — B should still be 0.

clarify.question: What does a wallet start with?
What should I print?
clarify.answer: Both balances, as (A's balance, B's balance).

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.

why_line: balance lives on the class and add changes Wallet.balance — there's only one balance, shared by every wallet, so B reads the 4 too.

explain.rule: Wallet.balance is the whiteboard in the kitchen: write 4 on it for wallet A, and wallet B — reading the same board — says 4 as well.
explain.bridge: So where should each wallet keep its own balance?

fix.rule: self.balance = 0 in __init__ gives each new wallet its own label; self.balance += n writes only on this wallet's label.

walk.gloss: Make wallet A — __init__ gives it its own balance of 0.
Make wallet B — its own balance of 0 too.
Add n to A's balance only.
